text: Why is an ambiguous grammar fatal rather than merely untidy?
choices: Ambiguous grammars cannot be parsed by any algorithm, so no implementation is possible.
Parsers built from ambiguous grammars run in exponential time on all inputs.
The ambiguity propagates into the tokenizer, which can no longer classify operators.
It does not determine the meaning of its own language — `2 + 3 * 4` could be 14 or 20 depending on which derivation the parser found.
explanation: Two distinct derivation trees for one string means two meanings, and a specification that does not say which is not a specification. The fix is not an annotation saying `*` binds tighter — grammars have no such mechanism — but restructuring so that only the intended tree is derivable: one level per precedence tier, loosest binding at the top.
